title: Siegard intent material
description: The frontmatter of one file of material read from a target's declared tests — what the source should do, where survey material reads what it does. «Every fact line of intent material names a test the material read and a file of the source it governs, and a line that names no test or no governed file is refused» (SPEC-005 R9). The body carries the six headings survey material carries, in the same order: `## Facts`, `## Answers`, `## Vocabularies`, `## Upstream artifacts`, `## Outside the domain`, `## Observed and not decided here`. A fact line is a top-level bullet (`- `) under the first four headings, naming in backticks the test it was read at and each file of `files` it governs; an indented bullet belongs to the fact above it. `bin/trace.py --survey` holds the file to this contract, and `--ledger` reads the governed files on each fact line to say which files each candidate node is read against. A heading with nothing to say carries the line `None.`.

contract_version.description: Which contract this material was written against.

target.description: The key of `siegard.json`'s `targets` the paths below are spelled from. Its declared tests are what `tests` may list.

tests.description: Every test the material read, spelled from the target source root, each one the target's declared test scope holds. A test is where a fact was read and never a file an adoption judges.

files.description: Every file of the source a fact governs, spelled from the target source root, none of them a declared test. The adoption's file set is this list, and each file's judge is handed the nodes the facts governing it landed in.

read_outside_area.description: Any other file opened to say which source file a test governs, with why, one line each. Read, never material: no fact is attributed to it.
